'''Øystein Linnebo''' (born 1971) is a [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[philosophy|philosopher]]. As of 2020 he is currently employed in the Department of Philosophy at the [[University of Oslo]], having earlier held a position as Professor of Philosophy at [[Birkbeck College]], [[University of London]]. He is a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gruppe 3: Idéfag|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27639|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=Norwegian|access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref>

==Career==
Linnebo earned his [[Master of Arts|MA]] in Mathematics from the [[University of Oslo]] in 1995 and his [[PhD]] in Philosophy at [[Harvard University]] in June 2002.

Linnebo's primary areas of concentration are [[philosophy of logic]], [[philosophy of mathematics]], [[metaphysics]], as well as [[philosophy of language]] and [[philosophy of science]]. He is known for his numerous publications in many top international journals in his field including: ''The Review of Symbolic Logic'', ''[[Dialectica]]'', ''[[The Journal of Philosophy]]'', ''[[Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic]]'' as well as editing a special edition of ''[[Synthese]]''.<ref name="hf">{{cite web|url=http://www.hf.uio.no/ifikk/english/people/aca/oysteinl|title=Øystein Linnebo - Department of Philosophy, Classics, History of Art and Ideas|publisher=hf.uio.no|access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> Additionally, he is the author of the articles "Plural Quantification" and "Platonism in the Philosophy of Mathematics" in the ''[[Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy]]''.<ref name="stanford">{{cite web|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/plural-quant|title=Plural Quantification (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)|publisher=plato.stanford.edu|access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="stanford2">{{cite web|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/platonism-mathematics|title=Platonism in the Philosophy of Mathematics (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)|publisher=plato.stanford.edu|access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> He is also an "Area Editor" for philosophy of mathematics on ''[[PhilPapers]]''.<ref name="philpapers">{{cite web|url=http://philpapers.org/help/about.html|title=About - PhilPapers|publisher=philpapers.org|access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

In addition to being a Professorial fellow at the Northern Institute of Philosophy, [[University of Aberdeen]] he has also been awarded many grants. Most recently he led a research project as part of a [[European Research Council|European Research Council Starting Grant]] entitled "Plurals, Predicates, and Paradox: Towards a Type-Free Account" which ran from January 2010 until December 2013.<ref name="hf2">{{cite web|url=https://www.hf.uio.no/ifikk/english/research/projects/ppp|title=Plurals, Predicates and Paradox - ERC Starting Grants Research Project (completed) - Department of Philosophy, Classics, History of Art and Ideas|publisher=hf.uio.no|access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

In 2018, he published ''Thin Objects: An Abstractionist Account'', an [[Abstractionism (philosophy of mathematics)|abstractionist]] approach to [[abstract object theory|thin objects]].

Since 2022, he is visiting professor at the [[Università della Svizzera italiana|University of Italian Switzerland]].
